expected_reconciliation_findings.where: CIM FY24 revenue 31.8 vs management accounts 30.9
expected_reconciliation_findings.description: The CIM reports FY24 revenue of 31.8. Management accounts issued afterwards report 30.9, restated to exclude a divested clinic services line. Gross profit and adjusted EBITDA move with it.
expected_reconciliation_findings.expected_detection: Two live observations for revenue FY24 from different documents, differing by 0.9. Both must be retained and shown side by side; neither may be silently preferred.

expected_reconciliation_findings.where: workbook, operating expenses presented on two axes
expected_reconciliation_findings.description: Operating costs are presented both by nature (personnel, non-personnel) and by function (product, S&M, G&A) for the same cost base. Each axis sums to total opex on its own.
expected_reconciliation_findings.expected_detection: Summing every expense row gives twice total operating expenses. Each axis must reconcile to the total independently, and only one may be used in any calculation.

expected_reconciliation_findings.description: A check row references a named range that does not exist, so it reports an error permanently while being displayed as though it were a working control.
expected_reconciliation_findings.expected_detection: A check that cannot be evaluated must be reported in words as not evaluable. Rendering it blank, as a dash, or as an error code lets it read as decoration.

notes: Extraction is scored against what each document literally says, defects included. Correcting a figure during extraction is a failure, not a help.
Reconciliation is scored against expected_reconciliation_findings. One finding is not a genuine error and must stop being raised once explained (see docs/DECISIONS.md #011).
Pages listed in pages_requiring_ocr_or_flagging hold figures that text extraction cannot recover. Reporting them as unread is correct; reporting them as empty is not.
